verdicts.evidence: src/TreeHash.jl:47 now reads `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue  # git tracks no empty directory`, exactly the hint's suggested fix, replacing the always-false `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip)) && continue`. Verified with a standalone Julia run that `_nonempty` returns a Bool and `false || continue` now skips. A new test/treehash.jl compares `TreeHash.tree_hash` against real `git write-tree` on a tree containing a recursively-empty subdirectory (matching git's SHA exactly) and against a directory containing only an empty subdirectory (matching git's canonical empty-tree id `4b825dc6...`). `julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'` shows "tree hash vs git write-tree | 2 2" passing.

class_surfaces.evidence: `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip)) && continue` (always false) changed to `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue` — the only site the finding names as carrying the bug.

verdicts.evidence: src/Witnesses.jl:167 now reads `f == 0 && blocked !== nothing && return WitnessResult(name, :blocked, p, f, e, blocked)` in the `e > 0` branch (was `blocked === nothing || return ...`), so a witness with `f>0` and `e>0` together now falls through to `:broken` with a reason naming both counts ("$f assertion(s) failed AND ... an assertion threw"). Both docstrings (WitnessResult ~32-33, run_one ~145-148) were reworded to state `:blocked` requires zero failures. test/witnesses.jl adds `blocked_but_failed.jl` reproducing the finding's exact repro (a failing @test plus an erroring @test under a `# blocked:` header) and asserts `st["blocked_but_failed.jl"] == :broken` and that the reason names the failed assertion count; `Pkg.test()` shows "witness runner | 13 13" passing.

class_surfaces.evidence: WitnessResult docstring now: ":blocked` (the file declares `# blocked: <reason>`, reported its counts, errored and failed nothing; a run that reported no counts is `:broken`)" — drops the false "was never seen to fail" implication and requires f==0.

run_one docstring now: "or `:blocked` (it errored, failed nothing, and carries a `# blocked: <reason>` header; one that also failed is `:broken`, its reason naming both counts, and so is one that reported no counts at all — an exit or a crash — header or not)".
the `e > 0` branch now gates `:blocked` on `f == 0`; a witness that also failed returns `:broken` with a reason naming both counts, per the hint.
